result.title: LATER: Learning Action-Conditioned Temporal Evidence Retrieval for Predictive World Models
result.summary: Early interactions can reveal physical properties that later observations no longer show. These properties can still gov- ern the effects of future actions. Inspired by the distinction between retention and selective readout in working mem- ory and cognitive science, we introduce LATER, an action- conditioned world model built on CF-JEPA. LATER stores completed real transitions in partitioned memories that remain fixed during candidate rollouts. A response bridge queries these memories using the current state and candidate action, while multi-cut auxiliary supervision trains the memory writ- ers. On distracted Two-Stage PushT, LATER raises terminal success from 15.5% to 25.0% over reconstructed CF-JEPA. In a separate comparison across six models and two scratch- training seeds, LATER achieves the lowest mean physical readout error in both clean and distracted views, reducing along-push mean absolute error (MAE) under distractors by 20.2% relative to CF-JEPA. Controlled history interventions show that later predictions depend on earlier physical evi- dence even when query observations and actions are fixed, with larger effects during pushing than waiting.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 LATER，一个基于 CF-JEPA 的动作条件世界模型：将已完成的真实转移写入分区记忆，并在候选动作 rollout 中保持固定，由 response bridge 结合当前状态与候选动作选择性读取，并用 multi-cut 辅助监督训练记忆写入；在 Two-Stage PushT 上评估成功率、物理量读取误差及历史证据依赖。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「保留与选择性读取」的记忆分区、固定缓存及早期视觉证据干预，可能为 LVR 的视觉证据筛选、跨步状态保持和缓存/读取结构提供核查线索；但研究的是世界模型预测而非 VLM 推理状态生成，联系需进一步判断。
